title: Certainty of one’s justification is not the same kind as certainty of revealed articles of faith
source_text: XXVI. Inde vero manifestum est certitudinem quam quis habet de sua coram Deo justificatione, non esse plane ejusdem generis & rationis, cum certitudine illa quam habemus de Fidei articulis, & dogmatibus quae Deus in Verbo suo revelavit. Haec enim in fideli omnino necessaria est. Nec quisquam potest fidelis permanere, & pro tali merito haberi; & tamen dubitare de fidei articulis, exempli causa, An Jesus sit Christus, & Dei filius; &, An mortui sint olim resurrecturi. Cum tamen, ut jam dictum, omnis qui dubitat an sit justificatus, & acceptus Deo ad vitam aeternam, non statim propterea judicandus sit carere vera fide, nec esse in Dei gratia, ut nec ullo modo potest pro dogmate fidei haberi, quod hic, vel ille sit justificatus, & gratiae divinae particeps.
pass_a_gloss: From this it is plain that the certainty which someone has concerning his justification before God is not altogether of the same kind and reason as that certainty which we have concerning the articles of faith and the dogmas God has revealed in his Word. For the latter is altogether necessary in a believer. Nor can anyone remain a believer and deservedly be held as such and yet doubt concerning the articles of faith—for example whether Jesus is the Christ and Son of God, and whether the dead will one day rise. Whereas, as already said, everyone who doubts whether he is justified and accepted by God unto eternal life is not for that reason immediately to be judged to lack true faith or not to be in God’s grace; nor can it in any way be held as an article of faith that this or that person is justified and a partaker of divine grace.
pass_b_english: Dogmatic certainty about revealed articles is necessary to remaining a believer.
Personal certainty that I am justified is not the same genus and is not itself a dogma of faith.
